summary: Comprehensive testing of Kids IQ Test v2 (adaptive sessions, PDF, certificates, brain games, notifications, progress, admin). Backend: 34/34 pytest tests passed covering all v2 endpoints. Frontend: full E2E verified - login, notification bell (badge shows unread count), games hub (7 cards), memory match game loads, adaptive assessment flow (15Q for 9-12), timer visible, session-based /api/sessions/start + submit, report page with KPIs (Accuracy/Speed/Consistency/Attention), radar chart, category breakdown, strengths + growth areas, AI insights section, PDF download working (%PDF- magic bytes). Certificates page loads. Progress page renders XP/Stars/Badges cards, timeline, category breakdown when data exists. Assessment PDF downloads with correct content-type. Certificate PDF verified via pytest (correct-answer fixture triggers cert creation).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 745 lines - large single file. Consider splitting into routers: auth, children, sessions, certificates, games, notifications, admin. Per code review guideline files >700 lines should be split.

assessment_engine.compute_weighted_score has a subtle bug in strengths/growth_areas: the list comprehension `growth = [c for c, _ in sorted_cats[-3:][::-1] if _['score'] < 70]` uses `_` as an actual variable (not throwaway). Works but style is confusing.
PDF endpoints /api/assessments/{id}/pdf and /api/certificates/{id}/pdf use ObjectId(a['child_id']) without try/except - malformed data would produce 500 instead of 400/404 (defensive).
generate_ai_report catches all exceptions with bare `except Exception` and swallows; consider narrower catch + logging (already logs exception).
In sessions/submit, `durations = payload.durations if len(payload.durations) == len(ordered_qs) else [q['estimated_time'] for q in ordered_qs]` correctly handles mismatched durations. Good.
Certificate creation is gated at overall_score >= 50; this is a business rule. Frontend shows 'no certificates' state gracefully when score < 50.
assessment_engine.build_adaptive_session uses global random module - if concurrent sessions with same seed occur, results could be non-deterministic across processes, but seed=None default is fine.
Missing rate limiting on /api/auth/login and /api/auth/register - no brute-force lockout as mentioned in playbook (5 fails). Optional per playbook, not part of current PRD.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all critical flows verified: login, navbar notif, games hub with 7 cards, memory match loads, full assessment flow, report page with KPIs/radar/categories, PDF download, progress page, certificates page)
